Vets who told me the same things I easily found on chatgpt.
Textbook vets, a bit like those who graduate by learning everything by heart, and then go get drunk after the exam.
You are proof that a degree doesn't make you sensitive and therefore intelligent.
My cat lost her life after a year.
We had to put her down (by another vet) because
for months, according to the results of the numerous visits performed at this facility, she seemed healthy as a fiddle.
Although your doctor recommended various treatments,
at most, he was aware of the fact that, for alternate months, my cat had been experiencing similar problems.
Over the past few days, I've tried to contact the doctor, informing him that my cat, despite having been administering cortisone, antibiotics, and anticonvulsants for about a week,
was showing no signs of improvement and had been ignoring my messages for several days.
A €900 CT scan wouldn't have solved anything for my cat because, given their lack of seriousness, it was too late to intervene.
The CT scan would have completed and provided a clearer diagnosis, but it was too late.
My cat was having three seizures a day, was aggressive, fearful, and unresponsive to stimuli (always during the administration of her medications).
I was advised to entertain her with toys, scratching posts, CBD, etc.
Zero professionalism.
Degrading environment, because for a location like this, Milan is a bit squalid.
To be a veterinarian, simply liking animals isn't enough.
I strongly advise against this clinic.
Avoid it like the plague if you don't want to see your pets reach the point of no return.

I wrote a detailed review about what happened and what I'm going through three years later, but Google won't let me publish it (among the reasons why it's negative). I'll just say that my dog ​​was neutered at 11 months old with an undescended testicle, and from then on, he started having serious problems. Veterinarian Capasso is highly discouraged.

Update to my review.
We finally got a diagnosis thanks to a truly excellent neurologist. My dog ​​was neutered at this clinic by Dr. Capasso. When I asked if it wasn't too early, given his almost 11-month-old age, he replied that he was absolutely ready (already developed) for the surgery. He had an undescended testicle in his groin. After the neutering, which he was perfectly ready for, as Dr. Capasso said, the dog immediately started having problems (peeing in the house, which he had long ago learned not to do, compulsive thirst, anxiety). At first, they hypothesized it was cystitis. Since the problem persisted even with Meloxidyl, they prescribed Relaxigen, saying it was a behavioral problem (all over the phone). As the problem persisted, I went to the clinic where I met Dr. Capasso, whom I asked for clarification on what could have happened to my dog, given that after the neutering he was having problems that he hadn't had before. Dr. Capasso treated me in a dismissive manner, as if I were a damned nuisance, nervously pleading with me to show up the following Tuesday for a bladder ultrasound, as if to please me. As I was leaving, I heard him telling me to go fuck myself behind my back. Of course, I didn't show up the following week. No one called me. I changed clinics. From there, my dog's condition escalated, leading to seizures. No one could figure out what was wrong. Test after test, all perfect. In two years, my dog ​​had six seizures, all following external factors that were stressful for him. Fears he hadn't had before. Anxiety about everything. He was prescribed a bunch of natural tranquilizers, which worked for a while but then faded into nothing. Until I turned to this neurologist, who, after reviewing videos of the seizures and examining the dog, finally reached the diagnosis: paroxysmal seizures due to his anxiety, which had now reached the point of extreme anxiety, leading him to have these seizures. I was explained that castration must be evaluated on a case-by-case basis. In dogs that already have an insecure nature, it is not recommended. Obviously, the retained testicle in the groin had to be removed, but it would have been better to leave the other one so as not to deprive a dog, already with this nature, of all the testosterone. This is also why we wait at least a year to better assess the dog's temperament. My 4-year-old puppy is currently taking medication for anxiety and seizures. We started with the lowest dosage, and we'll see if it's worth increasing over time. It will be a truly long and complicated journey. Could all this suffering have been avoided for him and for us, his family, who love him like a son? Yes!
I wanted to share this experience of mine also to encourage all of you parents of furry children to turn to serious and competent veterinarians who aren't just looking out for their wallets, but also for the best of your pet, evaluating their individual case. If you feel (as I did) that the doctor is too hasty, overbearing, or arrogant, or even if you're not convinced by him, listen to your instincts and turn to another doctor without hesitation. Today, I can say that even a seemingly routine procedure, often recommended like castration, can turn into a never-ending nightmare for you and your pets. A good vet knows when to do it or not. Don't take it lightly.

I brought in a blackbird injured by a cat, not knowing what to do and having to go to work. The vet told me she didn't want to take it in (she should call the local police) and to leave it in a park.
Apparently, vets are for the money, not to help animals. I understand, but I disagree.

I brought my cat Krystal in very serious condition. Despite everything, the first to respond was Dr. Lorenzo Capasso, and then the entire staff, who offered their services with rare humanity, especially after other large clinic chains had turned us down because they don't accept desperate cases, prioritizing business. They supported us through our greatest pain, treating us with respect and dignity, even financially. Here, you can truly see that animals come first. Empathic professionals tried to do everything they could, clarifying the situation for us. Thank you so much for your professionalism and compassion.
I highly recommend this clinic as a place to bring our beloved family pets.

I'd like to give Dr. Dominione more than 5 stars. He's always there, available, loving, and empathetic, attentive, and unique, thanks also to his exceptional professionalism.

Thank you, Doctor.

I've been going there for several years, and until recently, I was always told during various routine visits and vaccinations that my dogs' teeth were perfect! Well, my dog ​​lost 4 teeth, I went to another facility where they told me that unfortunately both my dogs, especially the male, have acute periodontitis and need emergency surgery! They say that to have gotten this far, my dog ​​has had this infection for years! But I ask, how the hell do you check them? Why tell me the teeth are perfect if they are full of tartar? Furthermore, the very hasty attitude during the last visit regarding possible kidney stones left me stunned. You obviously lost a customer! It's a shame, but this dental issue is truly serious!
Thank you!

The best clinic in Milan.
Dr. Dominione is a marvelous professional, very knowledgeable and humble.
Prices more than honest.

The best clinic in Milan.
Dr. Dominione is an exceptional professional.
Very honest prices.

It's the absolute best clinic in Milan. I'll always be grateful for saving my little Stellina when she was about to give birth and she and her babies were dying. Doctors Bianchi and Coiatelli are absolutely fantastic.

Unfortunately (although it's already happening), pet owners will increasingly give up on caring for their beloved pets. And dear professionals, let's not ask ourselves why.

The unfortunate thing, which isn't really unfortunate, is finding yourself having to bring your furry friend to these five-star emergency rooms on a Sunday.

Chosen far from home because it was quieter than other clinics, which are always crowded and impersonal, for my cat's health problem, he said goodbye to me after a visit, an x-ray, and an injection, with €200 less in my pocket.

The costs are decidedly exorbitant, even if (a trend exclusive to Milan), justified by the word "weekend." Thanks anyway to Dr. Coiatelli and his colleagues for the service and availability provided.

I had a serious problem with my cat; he needed intensive care at another facility. Dr. Capasso showed zero empathy, mainly concerned with the bureaucratic aspects and payment. For this reason, I strongly advise against it.

Dramatic experience with Dr. Capasso.
In September 2024, my 15-year-old cat presented vomiting, weight loss, and a creatinine level of 2.1, signs of early kidney failure. The doctor dismissed everything superficially, describing her as "like a 5-year-old cat." Eight months later, with new, obvious symptoms, he decided not to pursue further tests, postponing the diagnosis for a month. Three weeks later, she was admitted to the emergency room: acute, chronic kidney failure, now irreversible. Other veterinarians acknowledged that the decline had begun at least a month before her admission and that, with timely treatment, she could have been saved. Every day with her is a gift now, knowing that tomorrow she could be gone.
Anyone who behaves like this shouldn't be holding the life of someone who gives us unconditional love and deserves genuine care in their hands. And for anyone who might want to justify themselves, I'd like to point out that, when informed of the seriousness of the situation, the doctor didn't even remember my cat. That says it all.

A special thanks goes to Doc Dominione for his professionalism and for reassuring me before performing a (very simple) procedure on my dog... I was the one who was terrified, not her 🥴... everything I was told was correct... great professionalism and experience!
A heartfelt thank you to the entire wonderful team (unfortunately, I don't remember all their names) for their kindness, professional preparation, and all the patience they have with us, the owners of WONDERFUL SOULS, who, at times, are unbearable with a thousand fears and anxieties! THANK YOU from the bottom of my heart 💖
Dr. Bianchi treated us very badly and invited us to go back to the vet Romanelli Marina. It doesn't seem ethical or professional to me.

They've been the clinic that's cared for my two cocker spaniels for a while now! They're always attentive to the animals' needs and have veterinarians specializing in various fields, so whenever your pet has a specific issue, you can always find the right vet. I especially appreciate the skill of Dr. Sala, who was able to put my elderly dog ​​to sleep perfectly for scaling; he had no trouble waking up. Highly recommended veterinary team!
An exceptional and caring doctor unlike any I've ever seen. A doctor who's on the ball. Fast, fair in her pricing, and very reassuring.

Thanks to all the staff for their expertise, kindness, and dedication in welcoming and caring for our cat Minerva.
Highly recommended clinic, a must-visit when looking for answers and specific care.
After a long search for a vet to neuter our dog and keep up with his vaccinations, this vet was recommended to us, and we're very happy. They're honest, have fixed prices, and are always available.
Dr. Assalini is extremely kind and knowledgeable. He treated my cat with care and kindness, solving a problem that had been misdiagnosed elsewhere. I entrust my cat to him with great confidence.

We went to the emergency room because our dog was in a very serious condition. Another day, Pluto wouldn't have made it, but the doctor was excellent, and her confidence in handling the situation made us feel much more at ease. Pluto is doing great now and is continuing his treatment. I thank Dr. Marta, who saved him and was very kind. ❤️ HIGHLY RECOMMENDED CLINIC ⭐️
It's quite clear that their primary concern isn't the animal's health, but rather money. In my opinion, they also lack a bit of empathy and kindness towards animals and their owners.

Even though I live outside Milan, I always take my beloved pets to the Sempione clinic. The staff is professional and courteous. They have a team of trained and specialized doctors who always take care of all the animals. I have been lucky …
